alt: A table with one row per number of signs and one column per site. Row 1 starts as each site's own profit. Each later cell adds a site's profit to the best cell of the previous row among sites far enough to the left, found by a pointer that only moves right. Cells with no legal way show a dash. The largest cell is the answer.

steps.caption: With one sign, the best profit at each site is that site's own profit, so row 1 is `[3, 5, 6, 3, 4, 2]`. The sites are sorted by position `x`: 1, 2, 5, 7, 9, 13. A gap of 4 must separate any two signs.
Row 2, site 0 (x = 1). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = -3, so there is no way to end here with 2 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 2, site 1 (x = 2). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = -2, so there is no way to end here with 2 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 2, site 2 (x = 5, profit 6). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 1; the best row 1 cell among them is 3, at site 0. So the cell is 3 + 6 = 9.
Row 2, site 3 (x = 7, profit 3). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 3; the best row 1 cell among them is 5, at site 1. So the cell is 5 + 3 = 8.
Row 2, site 4 (x = 9, profit 4). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 5; the best row 1 cell among them is 6, at site 2. So the cell is 6 + 4 = 10.
Row 2, site 5 (x = 13, profit 2). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 9; the best row 1 cell among them is 6, at site 2. So the cell is 6 + 2 = 8.
Row 3, site 0 (x = 1). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = -3, so there is no way to end here with 3 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 3, site 1 (x = 2). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = -2, so there is no way to end here with 3 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 3, site 2 (x = 5). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = 1, so there is no way to end here with 3 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 3, site 3 (x = 7). No earlier site with a legal cell sits at or left of x - 4 = 3, so there is no way to end here with 3 signs: the cell is `-`.
Row 3, site 4 (x = 9, profit 4). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 5; the best row 2 cell among them is 9, at site 2. So the cell is 9 + 4 = 13.
Row 3, site 5 (x = 13, profit 2). The pointer `p` has folded in every site at or left of x - 4 = 9; the best row 2 cell among them is 10, at site 4. So the cell is 10 + 2 = 12.
Every row is filled. The largest cell is 13, in row 3, site 4. That is the program's answer.
